events.title: C++14 standardized
events.summary: ISO published C++14 in December 2014 — a minor but widely used update adding generic lambdas, `std::make_unique`, and digit separators.
events.about: C++14 polished C++11 rather than reinventing it: `auto` lambda parameters, return type deduction for functions, and binary literals made daily code shorter. Compilers shipped C++14 support quickly, making it the practical baseline for new C++ projects after 2015.

narrative.whyChosen: C++14 fixed rough edges in C++11 that every production codebase hit immediately.
narrative.whyImportant: `make_unique` and generic lambdas became idiomatic overnight.
narrative.problemSolved: C++11 left gaps — no `make_unique`, verbose lambdas — that slowed adoption.
